paper_metadata.title: Intermediate Qutrit-based Improved Quantum Arithmetic Operations with Application on Financial Derivative Pricing

summary: This paper proposes intermediate-qutrit decompositions for gate-based quantum arithmetic used in derivative pricing, reducing Toffoli decomposition depth from 7 to 3 and T-depth from 1 to 0. For the derivative-pricing benchmark, it reports a ternary CNOT cost and overall circuit depth of 162 million, and a Toffoli-count-30 success probability of about 0.4 versus 0.01 for the conventional decomposition, corresponding to about a 40% decrease in error probability.

experiments.description: Resource-estimation study of intermediate-qutrit decomposition for basic quantum arithmetic operations (addition/subtraction, multiplication/division, square root, exponential, arcsine) and their use in gate-based derivative pricing circuits; includes comparison against prior qubit-only Toffoli decomposition and a numerical 5×3 multiplier example.

algorithm.variant: intermediate qutrit-based quantum arithmetic for derivative pricing

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Fixed-point binary registers for arithmetic; intermediate qutrits used only as temporary ternary states in Toffoli decomposition while keeping binary input/output. Derivative-pricing path loading and payoff evaluation use arithmetic subroutines (addition, multiplication, square root, exponential, arcsine).
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate resources and improve circuit depth/gate count for arithmetic subroutines used in quantum derivative pricing; application computes expected discounted payoff E(f) via amplitude estimation.

problem_instance.description: Derivative pricing benchmark from Chakrabarti et al. with a basket autocallable option example; paper also gives a 5×3 multiplier toy example for circuit verification.

dataset_specification.description: Basket autocallable with 3 underlyings, 5 payment dates, and a knock-in put option with 20 barrier dates (benchmark from prior work).

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Re-parameterization method for path loading; Gaussian path generation via VQE-based Gaussian operator; fixed-point arithmetic for payoff calculation; binary discretization of paths and payoffs.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Resource comparison against prior work; numerical simulation of 5×3 multiplier; success-probability analysis for Toffoli decomposition versus Toffoli count, with example at Toffoli count 30.

noise_model.noise_type: gate_error and amplitude-damping/relaxation error model for qutrits

speedup_claims.conditions: for derivative-pricing estimation via quantum amplitude estimation
speedup_claims.caveats: Claim refers to the amplitude-estimation subroutine in general; not specifically demonstrated in a hardware experiment here.

speedup_claims.conditions: using intermediate qutrit decomposition with no T gates
speedup_claims.caveats: Applies to the Toffoli decomposition used inside arithmetic circuits.

speedup_claims.factor: overall circuit depth reduced from 7 to 3
speedup_claims.conditions: for a single Toffoli gate decomposition
speedup_claims.caveats: Depth comparison is for the decomposed Toffoli gate, not the full derivative-pricing circuit.

speedup_claims.conditions: for a single Toffoli gate decomposition
speedup_claims.caveats: Counts refer to the decomposition of one Toffoli gate into two-qutrit gates.

speedup_claims.factor: approximately 40% decrease in probability of error
speedup_claims.conditions: for Toffoli count 30 in a circuit
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper also states the success probability is about 0.4 versus 0.01 for the conventional method at Toffoli count 30.

speedup_claims.baseline_method: prior work on derivative pricing with qubit-only Toffoli decomposition
speedup_claims.conditions: because no T gates are used in the proposed arithmetic circuits
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a resource-estimation claim, not a runtime benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Improved arithmetic resource counts via intermediate qutrits; Toffoli decomposition depth reduced from 7 to 3 and T-depth from 1 to 0; derivative-pricing subroutines retain asymptotic structure but with lower constant factors.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Monte Carlo pricing error O(M^-1/2) classically; quantum amplitude estimation gives O(M^-1) for the estimation subroutine.
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: Example benchmark reported as ternary CNOT-cost 162 million and overall circuit depth 162 million for derivative pricing; Toffoli decomposition uses 3 two-qutrit gates instead of 25 gates in conventional decomposition.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: The paper reports asymptotic resource reductions for arithmetic subroutines and a benchmark derivative-pricing circuit, but no end-to-end QPU demonstration. The main quantitative claim is a reduction of Toffoli decomposition depth from 7 to 3 and T-depth from 1 to 0, with a benchmark derivative-pricing estimate of 162 million ternary CNOTs / 162 million depth.
limiting_factors: No hardware execution on a quantum processor
Quadratic Monte Carlo speedup only for amplitude estimation, which is not enough to establish practical advantage under Hoefler-style constant-factor analysis
Derivative pricing still depends on expensive state preparation / path loading
Intermediate qutrit hardware is not standard and is not demonstrated here
The paper is primarily a resource-estimation and circuit-design study

notes: No specific QPU or simulator backend is named; Google Colab is mentioned only for simulation of the multiplier example, so hardware.type is inferred as not_specified rather than a real device.
The paper reports resource formulas and example depths/counts, but not a single universal qubit count for the full derivative-pricing circuit; num_qubits is therefore left null.
Speedup order is inferred from the paper's discussion of amplitude estimation improving Monte Carlo convergence from O(M^-1/2) to O(M^-1).
The paper argues improved circuit depth and gate count, but does not demonstrate practical quantum advantage over classical pricing on a meaningful problem size.
The reported 40% reduction in error probability is for a Toffoli decomposition benchmark, not an end-to-end finance application.

experiments.description: Standalone Toffoli-gate decomposition benchmark using intermediate qutrits, compared against the conventional T-depth-1 decomposition.
key_results: Toffoli decomposition depth reduced from 7 to 3
3 two-qutrit gates replace 7 one-qubit + 16 two-qubit gates
Probability of success at Toffoli count 30: ~0.4 vs ~0.01 conventional
Percentage decrease in probability of error: ~40%
